title: Russell US Style indexes — conditional quarter-end capping check effective at the open of 2027-12-31 (24% / 4.8%-above-48% test struck on the 2027-12-28 close), the second index family recapping into the same year-end close
source: EST: rule-derived by applying the family's OWN published rule, already extracted from primaries by four sibling ledgers in this calendar, to the December 2027 session calendar established from a primary by this proposer. THE RULE, as recorded verbatim in russell-style-quarter-end-capping-effective-2027-06-30.json from FTSE Russell's "Capping Methodology Guide" v5.4, September 2026 (capping-methodology-guide.pdf, HTTP 200, 652,008 bytes), section 4.8.6: every Russell US Style row reads price date "T-3", effective date "Last business day of each month", trigger "No company is greater than 24%, and all companies that have a weight greater than 4.8% in aggregate are no more than 48% of the index". THE DERIVATION WAS TESTED, NOT ASSERTED: T-3 sessions back from the last business day reproduces FTSE Russell's own published 2026 quarter-end cut-offs exactly — for a Tue 2026-06-30 effective the guide's schedule table publishes 25 June 2026, and 06-29/06-26/06-25 counts back to it; for a Thu 2026-12-31 effective it publishes 28 December 2026, and 12-30/12-29/12-28 counts back to it. Applied to December 2027, whose last business day is Fri 2027-12-31 — established from nyse.com/markets/hours-calendars, fetched direct by this proposer 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 109,180 bytes), whose own footnote reads "Because the holiday falls on Saturday, January 1, 2028, no New Year's Day holiday is observed" — the sessions count back 12-30, 12-29, 12-28, so the cut-off is the Tue 2027-12-28 close and the check is effective at the open of Fri 2027-12-31. Filed estimate on the four counts this family always records: a proposal is estimate by contract, this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep, the confirmed-tier prefixes in market-events-data.ts have no member for an index owner's own published methodology, and the FAQ's own schedule table carries "NOTE: Dates may be subject to change. Clients will be notified of any changes." Conditional by construction — the FAQ says "If no breach is identified, no changes are made." Checked 2026-09-09
notes: PROPOSED by the sp-select-sector-secondary-reweight-2027-12-31 initial research (2026-09-09), found by enumerating that event's own corridor. THE GAP IS EXACT AND MECHANICAL: this calendar tracks russell-style-quarter-end-capping-effective- for 2026-09-30, 2026-12-31, 2027-03-31 and 2027-06-30 and stops. 2027-12-31 is the quarter-end the proposer's event lands on and it was simply missing. WHY IT MATTERS TO THE PROPOSER: the sp-select-sector-secondary-reweight-2026-12-31 ledger's one genuinely distinctive corridor finding was that TWO index families' conditional recaps clear on the same year-end close — Select Sector's after the close, Russell's at the open — which it called a simultaneity note and explicitly not a size note. That observation is only visible because the 2026 pair are both on the calendar. For 2027 the Select Sector half is tracked and the Russell half is not, so the same corridor reads as quiet when it is not. Filing this restores the comparison rather than making a new claim. ONE DERIVATION DELIBERATELY NOT MADE HERE, so a taking lane does not inherit a guess: the QUARTERLY REVIEW dates (style capping cut-off and review effective open) are NOT derived in this proposal. The 2027-06-30 sibling's rule for them — review effective open = the Monday after the quarter's implementation Friday, cut-off = that Monday minus 12 calendar days — reproduces all four published 2026 columns, but December 2026's implementation Friday is the SECOND Friday (11 Dec, giving a 14 Dec review effective) where March and September use the third; this proposer did not fetch the FAQ schedule table itself and will not extend an inconsistent-looking pattern by hand. The T-3 quarter-end derivation above is independent of that question and reproduces the December 2026 column directly, which is why this entry's DATE is the part being proposed. A taking lane should re-fetch the FTSE Russell FAQ and settle the review dates from the owner's own 2027 column. TWO CORRIDOR FEATURES A TAKING LANE SHOULD NOT REDISCOVER THE HARD WAY: 2027-12-31 is a full equity session carrying an OCC quarterly expiration, but it is ALSO a SIFMA-recommended bond early close (sifma-bond-early-close-2027-12-31) with the Federal Reserve Board shut (fed-board-closure-2027-12-31), so any forced print lands into a half-staffed tape — an E1-class execution note, not a trade. And the 2027-12-28 cut-off shares its session with fhfa-hpi-2027-12-28, the corridor's only `confirmed` entry. Low impact and market-structure only; conditional and usually does not fire; the proposer makes no claim that it will in December 2027 and no weight measured in 2026 forecasts a 2027 breach. Nothing here licenses an entry. The 2027-09-30 instance is the same gap, sits outside this proposer's corridor, and is deliberately NOT filed here.
